ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows a periodic square-wave signal x(t); the vertical axis marks amplitudes +1 and -1, and the horizontal axis is time t, marked with -T/2, 0, T/2. The waveform jumps between the two levels +1 and -1, and the durations of the positive half-cycle and negative half-cycle are equal. It can be seen from the image that this square wave satisfies half-wave symmetry: x(t+T/2) = -x(t). In the Fourier series of a periodic signal with half-wave symmetry, there are only odd harmonics and no even harmonics. Therefore, the second harmonic is an even harmonic, and its component is 0.

method.method_draft: First describe the plotted square wave: it is a periodic two-level signal taking +1 for half a period and -1 for the other half. From the equal positive and negative half-periods, identify half-wave symmetry, x(t+T/2) = -x(t). Use the standard Fourier-series result that half-wave symmetric signals contain only odd harmonics. Since the second harmonic is an even harmonic, its component is 0.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Uses the visual half-wave antisymmetry of the plotted 50% duty-cycle square wave rather than computing Fourier integrals term by term; this is the direct symmetry route to the zero second harmonic.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the waveform levels and timing from the image: x(t) alternates between +1 and -1 with equal-duration intervals, and the pattern repeats every T so that shifting the signal by T/2 flips its sign.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text to identify the requested quantity as the second harmonic component of the shown square wave.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Apply the Fourier-series symmetry rule: if a periodic signal has half-wave symmetry, x(t+T/2) = -x(t), all even harmonics vanish. Therefore the n=2 harmonic coefficient/component is zero.
